messages:
incident-bot: [P1] PagerDuty: Multi-region failover automation failed during traffic-shift from us-west-2 -> eu-central-1. Symptoms: high 5xx across hosted API, some Dedicated pools in us-west-2 are still receiving traffic. Paging oncall.

alex kim: acked. seeing spike in errors, rolling window shows 30% 5xx for generation endpoints in us-west-2 starting ~07:02 UTC. forwarding logs to thread.

maria gonzalez: I'm seeing repeated backend connect timeouts from the us-west-2 load balancer to model-serving nodes. Healthchecks toggling between healthy/unhealthy quickly.

devon li: likely a networking flake in the AZs. Cloud provider status shows "partial platform networking" in us-west-2a. Could be asymmetric routing causing LB healthchecks to fail.

sara patel: customer-impact: multiple self-serve customers report timeouts for long-generations and streaming stops. Dedicated customers on reserved pools in us-west-2 see degraded p95 latency and some token truncation.

alex kim: posting quick snapshot of metrics:
```
- 5xx rate (hosted/generate): 30% -> 12:20 UTC
- p95 latency (hosted/generate): 1.8s -> 5.2s
- Active sessions drained: 40% expected but logs show connections still established
```

maria gonzalez: runbook step 1: confirm traffic-shift status in orchestration: `rctl failover status --from us-west-2 --to eu-central-1 --id 2026-03-15T07:00`

network-bot: failover job 2026-03-15T07:00: state=running, step=drain-region, region=us-west-2, drained=43%, stuck_since=07:10UTC

devon li: runbook step 2: check DNS behavior. If DNS TTLs are long clients may cache old IPs and keep hitting us-west-2. Also check global LB weights.

sara patel: confirmed some customers have DNS TTL 300s but many internal caches are longer. We can't rely on instant DNS convergence here.

alex kim: I attempted to force more aggressive routing: `gcloud compute backend-services update --global --session-affinity=NONE --failover ...` but the platform automation didn't toggle the region to drain mode because the health-check controller marked many nodes as flapping.

maria gonzalez: logs from health-checker:
```
2026-03-15T07:07:21Z healthcheck: backend /model-v2/conv: response timeout 5s -> status=unhealthy
2026-03-15T07:07:25Z healthcheck: backend /model-v2/conv: response OK
2026-03-15T07:07:29Z healthcheck: backend /model-v2/conv: response timeout 5s -> status=unhealthy
```

devon li: flapping -> controller keeps re-adding backends, failover automation sees >50% healthy and refuses to complete drain. This leaves a window where traffic is still routed to us-west-2.

sara patel: customer impact assessment in progress. Early estimate: 18% of hosted traffic affected for 20 minutes, ~3 enterprise customers hit routing errors (temporary increased latency and timeouts).

alex kim: mitigation plan proposal: 1) Force-mark the us-west-2 region as "out-of-service" in the routing control plane to quarantine it. 2) Bump weights to eu-central-1 (target - fully shift) 3) For Dedicated customers, place temporary proxies in eu-central-1 to accept traffic for reserved pools.

maria gonzalez: step 1 done (manual override): `rctl routing override set region us-west-2 state OUT_OF_SERVICE --by oncall` - confirmed in control plane. However BGP/anycast caches still route some clients.

network-bot: BGP announcements updated: withdrawing anycast prefixes from us-west-2 regions at 07:18UTC.

devon li: checking edge logs: still seeing ~8% of traffic land on us-west-2 via certain ISP caches. Looks like DNS caching + ISP routing preference.

sara patel: started targeted support messages: posted to status page (incidents.redwood.ai) and opened a few L2 support tickets for affected enterprise customers with suggested temporary workarounds.

alex kim: observed unhealthy failover behavior: automation didn't escalate because it evaluates rolling averages; when healthchecks are flapping it assumes transient and retries. That logic needs a safety override for cross-region incidents. Filing a follow-up.

maria gonzalez: immediate extra mitigation: increase LB health-check threshold to be more permissive for 10 minutes so nodes don't flip repeatedly while we complete traffic shift. Command: `gcloud compute health-checks update ... --timeout 10s --unhealthy-threshold 5 --healthy-threshold 2` (rolled back after).

devon li: we're seeing streaming connections drop mid-response for a subset of clients. Suggest enabling fallback streaming relay in eu-central-1 for those sessions: `proxy-relay --enable-fallback --region eu-central-1`

sara patel: update for customers: added note indicating some long streaming sessions may have been truncated; we will retry those requests automatically for eligible built-in clients.

alex kim: still tracking two sticky issues: 1) ISP caches serving stale DNS -> some clients persist targeting us-west-2 IPs. 2) Some dedicated reserved pools tied to physical hosts in us-west-2 are stuck in partial health states preventing graceful failover.

maria gonzalez: for the dedicated pools we triggered a rolling reboot of the model-serving processes on 10 hosts (07:28 UTC) to break the flapping loop. That reduced healthcheck flips.

network-bot: control-plane state: failover job now progress=92% at 07:33UTC. Expected completion in ~2-3m once remaining persistent caches expire.

devon li: started handover notes for next oncall: leaving pinned checklist in incident channel and runbook pointers.

sara patel: customer impact summary for post-incident report (for internal use):
- window: 07:02 - 07:38 UTC
- affected surface: hosted API generate/stream, some Dedicated pools in us-west-2
- estimated affected traffic: peak 30% 5xx (most resolved by forced routing), residual 5-8% during cache expiry
- outage classification: partial regional degradation, not total outage
- immediate mitigations: routing override, BGP withdraw, lb health-check tuning, process restarts, proxy-relay fallback
- next steps: improve failover automation safety override, add runbook step for forcible region quarantine, document DNS caching risks in multi-region shifts

alex kim: handoff to night oncall @oncall-rotation at 07:40UTC. leaving notes: monitor residual 5xx, watch for delayed customer reports, follow up on postmortem owner (maria).

oncall-rotation: ack. thanks. will monitor and escalate if residual >5% 5xx for more than 15m.

maria gonzalez: filing postmortem ticket with action items: 1) add automation escape hatch; 2) add ISP/dns-caching checklist; 3) adjust failover healthcheck logic; 4) run a simulated cross-region failover drill.

devon li: small note: metrics + tracing captured a weird pattern where KV cache invalidation didn't fully propagate during drain; include that in follow-up.

sara patel: closing incident thread but will update status page when postmortem is published. Great work on quick mitigations, team. :tada:

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-15-1875321234: state=resolved (07:38UTC). Postmortem assigned to maria gonzalez.
